definition: Recognizing spoken content from lip movements in silent video.
details: Recognizing spoken content from lip movements in silent video. Deep models achieve word-level decoding for accessibility and silent speech interfaces.

explainer.lead: Lipreading is recognizing spoken content from lip movements in silent video. It matters for accessibility and silent speech interfaces, where audio is unavailable.

tiers.eli5: It is reading what someone is saying by watching their mouth instead of listening to their voice.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train deep models to decode words from silent video for accessibility and silent interfaces. The pitfall is visual ambiguity: many mouth shapes look alike, so word-level decoding is difficult.
tiers.paperLevel: Lipreading is recognizing spoken content from lip movements in silent video; deep models achieve word-level decoding for accessibility and silent speech interfaces. The definition does not specify accuracy levels or model architectures.

explainer.example: A captioning system processes silent video of a speaker and outputs the words being mouthed.
